bachelor planning

BLS with a Management minor

A flexible liberal-studies family to compare when you want a useful bachelor’s and have credit in several subjects. The researched recipe supplies building blocks; your catalog and individual course placements still need a current map.

What makes this route worth exploring

  • Flexible electives
  • Prior-learning evaluation
  • Competency-based tuition terms
  • Required institutional work chosen to cover real gaps

What needs to be confirmed

  • Confirm your general-education catalog before using an older recipe.
  • Upper-level electives, minor requirements and institutional residency are separate checks.
  • The community recipe has inconsistent totals and is not an approved 120-credit basket.
  • The FAQ requires 30 UMPI credits, including 12 major credits with 9 upper-level; confirm the application to this minor-based degree.
  • UMPI states no fixed incoming-credit limit. Ninety possible outside credits is arithmetic for a 120-credit degree with 30 institutional credits, not a universal incoming cap.

Eligibility and your situation

  • Request evaluation of courses, exams, credentials and eligible military learning.
  • Confirm admission, location eligibility and current minor availability.

A practical sequence

  1. Lock the BLS, minor and catalog and obtain the requirement audit.
  2. Apply existing credit to GE, minor and separate upper-level blocks.
  3. Approve a nonduplicating outside basket while reserving institutional subsets.
  4. Complete approved external work and send official records.
  5. Finish required UMPI assessments and remaining minor/elective work.
  6. Reconcile the official degree audit and apply for graduation.

Your next useful actions

  • Collect all transcripts and credentials with dates.
  • Ask UMPI for your GEC version and remaining minor/upper-level requirements.
  • Build the missing course map before purchasing new work.

bachelor planning

BABA with a Project Management concentration

A business-core route for someone who wants management and project work on the degree. Compare remaining concentration assessments and useful certificate awards with the broader BLS route.

What makes this route worth exploring

  • Shared business core
  • Certificate bundles evaluated once
  • Competency-based terms
  • Project-artifact and prerequisite planning

What needs to be confirmed

  • Confirm current core and concentration requirements.
  • One certificate can produce multiple awards that overlap other learning.
  • New GE rules and required project artifacts can change the sequence.
  • The verified general bachelor rule is 30 UMPI credits, including 12 major credits with 9 upper-level.
  • No certificate award or concentration-specific outside mapping was freshly verified for this guide.

Eligibility and your situation

  • Consider readiness for writing, quantitative work and applied projects.
  • Obtain current certificate equivalencies rather than copying historical bundle totals.

A practical sequence

  1. Select concentration/catalog and inventory prior learning.
  2. Map GE, core, concentration and electives as one audit.
  3. Check certificate versions, outputs and duplicate groups.
  4. Reserve institutional major/upper-level work and required artifacts.
  5. Complete approved external work and transmit records.
  6. Finish UMPI assessments, degree audit and conferral.

Your next useful actions

  • Compare BABA and BLS using the same inventory.
  • Ask about current certificate awards and project artifacts.
  • Build a current requirement map before choosing subscriptions.

master planning

YourPace MA in Organizational Leadership

An organizational-leadership graduate family to investigate. UMPI undergraduates can ask about approved graduate substitutions before filling every institutional elective.

What makes this route worth exploring

  • Graduate competency-based terms
  • Conditional undergraduate-to-graduate substitutions
  • Useful institutional electives

What needs to be confirmed

  • Confirm current admission, curriculum and recognition for the intended use.
  • Undergraduate-to-graduate substitutions require exact course and student approval.
  • Historical substitution pairs do not provide a complete current master’s map.

Eligibility and your situation

  • Confirm an eligible bachelor’s and program-specific entry requirements.
  • Undergraduates need permission for graduate substitutions and later degree use.

A practical sequence

  1. Confirm purpose and current MAOL eligibility.
  2. Obtain the full graduate requirement list and term policies.
  3. Verify any approved undergraduate substitutions and prevent duplicates.
  4. Evaluate prior graduate transfer separately from undergraduate credit.
  5. Complete remaining graduate assessments and final-project requirements.
  6. Audit the master’s award and conferral.

Your next useful actions

  • Request current admission and requirement sheets.
  • If still an undergraduate, ask about current substitution pairs and permission.
  • Build the missing graduate course map before estimating terms.

Credit limits, degree placement, institutional-credit requirements, and professional eligibility are separate decisions. Use the current catalog and get the receiving school’s written confirmation.
